newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa ends weaker after late sell-off.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa ends weaker after late sell-off.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures ended broadly lower Monday, after a sustained failure to pierce key resistance prompted a late-session reversal, traders said.

The market drifted near unchanged for much of the day, but prices spiraled lower late in the session amid widespread speculative liquidation. December futures hit an early high of $1,375, but after once again failing below resistance at $1,380, the market quickly retreated.
Most-active December delivery fell $8 a tonne on the day, to $1,359, having ranged from $1,355 to $1,375. Second-month March was down $6, to $1,394, while the remaining months also eased $6.
The day's volume was estimated at 3,336 lots.

Dealers said continued uncertainty about the size of the Ivorian harvest confined cocoa prices to a relatively narrow, $30 range. While chartists did not rule out a sudden move outside the $1,350-1,380 span, they said only fresh crop news could provide the market with a more decisive direction.
-- Wendy Pollack, New York Commodities Desk +1 212 859 1640
